resources.string: Sonivell reads the songs inside these folders, including subfolders.
Sonivell needs ffmpeg to read and play your songs. Install it with: sudo apt install ffmpeg
No music found in your folders. Add a folder in Settings.
Space plays or pauses. Ctrl+Arrows change song and volume. Ctrl+F search, Ctrl+L lyrics, Ctrl+Q queue, Ctrl+M compact mode, Esc goes back.
SMART could not analyze your music on this computer.
Your sound server (PipeWire) is not receiving Sonivell\'s audio, so Bluetooth headphones and the volume panel won\'t get it. Fix: sudo apt install pipewire-alsa, then reopen the app.
Your sound server (PulseAudio) is not receiving Sonivell\'s audio, so Bluetooth headphones and the volume panel won\'t get it. Fix: sudo apt install libasound2-plugins, then reopen the app.
No music found in your folders. Add a folder in Settings › Library.
“%1$s” will be deleted. Your songs stay on the computer.
None of the songs in that file are in your folders
Everything happens on this computer: no account, no internet, nothing is sent anywhere.
Trains a small model on this computer with what you finish and what you skip. Smart queues lean towards your taste. Nothing leaves here.
%1$,d of %2$,d · keeps going in the background while Sonivell is open
New songs show up by themselves when they arrive in your folders
Searches the lyrics saved on this computer (next to the songs, in the lyrics folder and embedded lyrics you have opened).
Saves your playlists in Music/Playlists/Sonivell so other Linux players can see them
Animated bars over the cover in the player, from the sound Sonivell itself is playing. Nothing is recorded.
Choose the folder with your .lrc files, named like the songs (.lrc files next to the songs are always read)
The equalizer is ready: move the bands to hear the difference.
Sonivell reads the songs in the folders you choose. Nothing leaves your computer.
